raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes background issue [#52833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52833)

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM` both default to `True`. Once `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is set, MLA `kv_b_proj` weights are re-quantized online regardless of the precision the checkpoint asked for, and there is no per-model opt-out.

`kv_b_proj` holds `[W_UK; W_UV]`, which decompress the latent KV cache on every read, so the perturbation applies to the whole KV history rather than to a single GEMM. That is why the damage shows up first in long context — exactly the
regime where these defaults have not been validated.

Two data points:

- #48051 measures ~11% error per attention layer from this path, accumulating into repetition loops.
- On `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, MTP acceptance rate goes 0% -> 58.5% when the re-quantization is skipped (#52833).

This PR flips both defaults to `False`. Accuracy over speed until the kernels are validated in long context. Anyone who wants them still gets them with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=1` / `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1`.

## Changes

- `vllm/envs.py`: both dataclass annotations and both `os.getenv` defaults flip `True` -> `False`; the two "By default is enabled" comments now say what the flags do and why they are off.
- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_fp8.py`: `ENV_DEFAULTS` pins the new `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM` default.
- `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py`: `test_fp4_env_defaults` likewise.

## Test Plan

- tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_fp8.py
- tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py

## Test Result

Passed.

--end--

=======================================
History for ones who may be interested
=======================================
## Purpose

Fixes issue [#52833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52833)

This PR replaces [#48051](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48051)’s model-name guard with the generic rule:
```python
kv_b_proj.quant_config is not None
and isinstance(kv_b_proj.quant_method, UnquantizedLinearMethod)
```

When that condition is true, both AITER FP4BMM and FP8BMM re-quantization are disabled for the projection and MLA uses the existing BF16 BMM path.

The behavior remains unchanged for:
- fully BF16 models, where **quant_config** is null;
- projections with a real quantized method; and
- DeepSeek-V3-family Quark checkpoints whose intentional dynamic MXFP4
  attention path selects **QuarkLinearMethod**.

The current dispatch treats a BF16 weight as sufficient evidence that this online re-quantization is safe. That is not true for quantized checkpoints which explicitly exclude **kv_b_proj** to preserve it in high precision.

## Test Plan

### focused unit tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py
```

### gfx950 model validation

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1

serve_args=(
  /home/xuebwang/models/amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4
  --port 8000
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
  --trust-remote-code
  --tensor-parallel-size 8
  --enable-expert-parallel
  --linear-backend aiter
  --moe-backend aiter
  --tool-call-parser glm47
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
  --reasoning-parser glm45
  --max-model-len 262144
  --max-num-seqs 2
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
)
vllm serve "${serve_args[@]}"
```

## Test Result

```text
Mean acceptance length: 3.92
Accepted: 193
Drafted: 330
Avg Draft acceptance rate: 58.5%
Per-position acceptance rate: 0.909, 0.727, 0.545, 0.424, 0.318
```

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

nodes.body: Documentation preview: https://vllm--53123.org.readthedocs.build/en/53123/

@fxmarty-amd :

- `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4` isn't affected by this PR. It keeps re-quantization on every layer, only checkpoints that never opted in are denied. The guard looks at `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`, and that flag *is* the opt-in you mean: it's the thing that turns the exclusion into a bypass. `maybe_update_config` only switches it on for DeepSeek-V3-family fp4 checkpoints, so the two models go different ways:

| | `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4` | **`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` (model in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52833)** |
|---|---|---|
| `model_type` | `deepseek_v3` | `glm_moe_dsa` |
| `kv_b_proj` excluded | yes, all 61 layers | yes, 79 entries |
| `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` | `True` | `False` |
| `get_quant_method` | `QuarkLinearMethod` | `UnquantizedLinearMethod` |
| this PR | **allows, unchanged** | **denies — the fix** |

- `--quantization-config.targets` is complementary: an override only helps who already know a checkpoint is misquantized, while this fixes the default that GLM-5.2-MXFP4 MTP goes 0% → 58.5% with no flag.
- On silence: agree. The test now derives `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` from `maybe_update_config` instead of setting it by hand.
cc @BowenBao @ColinZ22
`dynamic_mxfp4_quant` has nothing to do with this PR afaik?
Correct, it's not in the diff. The guard only checks `isinstance(kv_b_proj.quant_method, UnquantizedLinearMethod)`

I fail to understand https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a60c66e3dcd563a293a9a3f54541e7405e95c82e/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py#L87-L112 that is FP4-specific,

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a60c66e3dcd563a293a9a3f54541e7405e95c82e/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L1112-L1124

Completely unrelated to:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a60c66e3dcd563a293a9a3f54541e7405e95c82e/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_ocp_mx.py#L145

I also fail to see the connection with FP8:

`self.is_aiter_triton_fp8_bmm_enabled` -> `_is_mla_bmm_requantization_allowed(kv_b_proj)` and how it would relate to `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`

> `--quantization-config.targets` is complementary

It is not complementary, it should be the proper long-term solution, removing all this aiter-specific logic. The current vllm behavior of silently quantizing layers by default without users opting in is the cause of issues as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48051.

@xuebwang-amd I would prefer for now, we just change the env variables of `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0` as when these two are enabled by default, they have not been validated well in long context. The part that they are quantizing seems to be very sensitive to accuracy changes.

Thanks @tjtanaa 
Yes, quantize `kv_b_proj` would probably impact accuracy, it perturbs the whole KV history on every read, which is exactly why it would surface in long context first. This can be seen from two measurements: #48051 reports ~11% error per attention layer accumulating into repetition loops, and on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 the MTP acceptance rate goes 0% → 58.5% once the requantization is skipped.
I understand the solution. This is also what @vllmellm and I pointed out in the background issue https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52833.

Let's do this first, accuracy over speed for now.

> @xuebwang-amd TJ's point is to switch:
> 
> https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a9993878cccc5b598d0b8934becf6fffb03e6fb/vllm/envs.py#L147-L148
> 
> to `False` by default.

OK, re-purpose of this PR to be turning off VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_*BMM by default for MLA accuracy first. PR title and description are updated as well.
Please have a review, thanks!  @tjtanaa @vllmellm @fxmarty-amd @AndreasKaratzas

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I think these `self.is_aiter_triton_fp8_bmm_enabled` / `self.is_aiter_triton_fp4_bmm_enabled` flags were precisely meant to bypass any exclusion rule, e.g. with https://huggingface.co/amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 - see my offline message

See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167 => these flags are enabled by default, silently turning on online quantization while users are unaware. This should be moved to use `--quantization-config.targets`.

Enabling silent online quantization that may have an impact on accuracy is not great IMO
